questions.question: A man lent out ₹14,000 at 5% and ₹19,000 at 6% simple interest per annum. His total income (in ₹) from the interest in 3 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest = (P₁ × effective rate 1) + (P₂ × effective rate 2)

Effective Rate = Rate × Time

Total Interest = (14000 × 15%) + (19000 × 18%)

Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = 5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹14,000, Rate 1 (R₁) = 5%, Time (T) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹19,000, Rate 2 (R₂) = 6%, Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6b38849eb7537aaee3f625f076f630ce22661a3f277efb1397ac53e379d2dd3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (14000 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = 140 × 15 = ₹2100

⇒ SI₂ = (19000 × 6 × 3) ÷ 100 = 190 × 18 = ₹3420

⇒ Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ Total Interest = 2100 + 3420 = ₹5520

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,520.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after T years is given by A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Effective Rate Method

For Simple Interest, the effective rate for T years is simply R × T%. Here, 5% for 3 years becomes a 15% flat interest rate on the principal.

⇒ r = 7

⇒ r = -37/2

⇒ Radius is 7 cm

⇒ h = 23 + 7 = 30 cm

**∴ r= 7 cm and h = 30 cm **

questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively, while pipe C alone can fill the empty tank in 8 minutes. If pipes A, B and C are opened together, then in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of tank = LCM(15, 20, 8) = 120 units.

Efficiency of A = −120/15 = −8; B = −120/20 = −6; C = 120/8 = +15.

Combined efficiency = 15 − 8 − 6 = 1 unit/min.

Total time = 120 / 1 = 120 minutes.

Time in hours = 120 / 60 = 2 hours.

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Pipe A empties in 15 min, Pipe B empties in 20 min, Pipe C fills in 8 min.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Pipes
 Time (min)
 Quantity (units)
 Efficiency
 
 

 A (Empty)
 15
 120
 −8
 
 

 B (Empty)
 20
 −6
 
 

 C (Fill)
 8
 15
 
 

⇒ Total Work (LCM of 15, 20, 8) = 120 units

⇒ Net efficiency of (A + B + C) = −8 − 6 + 15 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Total time taken to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time = 120 / 1 = 120 minutes

⇒ Time in hours = 120 / 60 = 2 hours

**∴ The correct option is C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Convention

Filling pipes (inlets) are assigned positive efficiency, while emptying pipes (outlets) are assigned negative efficiency.

Net Rate of Work

If multiple pipes work together, the net rate of work is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Unit Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide the total minutes by 60 (1 hour = 60 minutes).</p

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹1800, triple the profit is obtained than the profit that would have been obtained by selling it for ₹1350. The cost price (in ₹ ) of the article is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial profit be P. Then the new profit at the higher selling price is 3P.

Difference in profit = 3P − P = 2P

Difference in Selling Price = 1800 − 1350 = 450

⇒ 2P = 450 ⇒ P = 225

Cost Price = Selling Price − Profit = 1350 − 225 = 1125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price 1 (SP₁) = ₹1800

Selling price 2 (SP₂) = ₹1350

Profit at SP₁ = 3 × Profit at SP₂

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 SP₂ = 1350
 SP₁ = 1800
 
 

 P
 
 

 2P = 450
 
 

 Total Profit = 3P
 
 CP = 1350 − 225 = 1125

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be ₹x.

⇒ Profit obtained at SP₁ = 1800 − x

⇒ Profit obtained at SP₂ = 1350 − x

According to the given condition:

⇒ 1800 − x = 3 × (1350 − x)

⇒ 1800 − x = 4050 − 3x

⇒ 3x − x = 4050 − 1800

⇒ 2x = 2250

⇒ x = 1125

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1125.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. The basic formula to find the Selling Price after allowing a discount is: SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective single discount percentage can be quickly calculated using the formula: Effective Discount = (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a shopkeeper claims to sell his goods at the exact cost price but uses false weights, the actual profit percentage generated is given by: Profit % = (Error ÷ False Weight) × 100.

Discount allowed to customer = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

Profit = SP − CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost Price for shopkeeper (CP) = 2600 × (100 − 18) ÷ 100

⇒ CP = 2600 × 82 ÷ 100 = ₹2132

⇒ Selling Price of shopkeeper (SP) = 2800 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 2800 × 85 ÷ 100 = ₹2380

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27cd4fd1a5ecd25f1f425a05a8395ee0ca936355c86b597b6838d1328eaee6c6.png] 

⇒ Earnings = SP − CP

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. SP = MP − Discount.

Profit and Loss

Profit is earned when Selling Price (SP) is greater than Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP, and Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Discount

When two consecutive discounts x% and y% are given, the equivalent single discount is (x + y − xy ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A person bought a rectangular piece of land whose length and breadth are in the ratio 7 : 5. If the cost of fencing the land is ₹2,880 at the rate of ₹15/m, then what is the length of the land?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total perimeter = Total cost ÷ Rate = 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 m

Ratio of Length to Breadth = 7 : 5 ⇒ Perimeter in ratio parts = 2 × (7 + 5) = 24 parts

24 parts = 192 m ⇒ 1 part = 8 m

Length = 7 parts = 7 × 8 = 56 m

**∴ The correct answer is 56 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length and Breadth ratio = 7 : 5

Total cost of fencing = ₹2880

Rate of fencing = ₹15/m

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Perimeter = Total Cost ÷ Rate

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bde5b7e8a296fbe2e39399af384f2d49a4e6ee8373bfdd142ecf5d0e2b49ca39.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter = 2880 ÷ 15 = 192 m

⇒ Let the length be 7x and the breadth be 5x.

⇒ 2 × (7x + 5x) = 192

⇒ 2 × 12x = 192

⇒ 24x = 192

⇒ x = 192 ÷ 24

⇒ x = 8

⇒ Length = 7x = 7 × 8 = 56 m

**∴ The correct answer is 56 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area = Length × Breadth. The total cost of flooring is determined by multiplying the total area by the rate per square unit.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The length of the longest pole that can be placed inside a rectangular area is its diagonal. Formula: Diagonal = √(L² + B²).
